airport.name: El Calafate - Commander Armando Tola International Airport

summary: El Calafate - Commander Armando Tola International Airport (FTE) is the main gateway to Argentina's iconic Los Glaciares National Park and the famous Perito Moreno Glacier in Patagonia. The airport was renamed in honor of Commander Armando Tola, a local aviation pioneer. Located on the shores of Lago Argentino, it handles significant seasonal tourist traffic, especially during the Southern Hemisphere summer when visitors flock to the Patagonian ice fields.
faqs:
Q: How far is the airport from El Calafate town center?
A: The airport is approximately 21 km (13 miles) east of El Calafate, with a drive time of around 20-25 minutes depending on traffic and weather conditions.

Q: Which airlines fly into El Calafate Airport?
A: Aerolineas Argentinas, LATAM Argentina, and Jetsmart operate regular flights, with frequent connections to Buenos Aires and some seasonal regional services.

Q: Is the airport international or domestic only?
A: Despite its 'International' designation, most scheduled flights are domestic, though the facility can handle international charter operations, particularly during cruise season.

Q: Are there ATMs and currency exchange at the airport?
A: Yes, there are ATMs in the terminal, but bringing Argentine pesos from Buenos Aires is recommended as exchange rates and availability can be limited.
transport_tips: Authorized airport taxis and remise (private hire) services are available outside the terminal with fixed rates to El Calafate town, typically around ARS 3000-5000. Pre-booking a shuttle or hotel transfer is highly recommended during peak tourist season (November to March). Rental car agencies operate at the airport and can be useful for exploring the wider region independently.
local_tip: Pack your Perito Moreno glacier tour essentials in your carry-on; flights from Buenos Aires are frequently delayed or re-routed through other Patagonian cities due to strong westerly winds, so having essentials on hand makes unexpected overnight stops far more comfortable.
